bug_semantics: For non-export builds, NextChat's Next.js response-header rule grants Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to the API surface. The current rule also grants every method and request header, so JavaScript from an attacker-controlled origin can pass preflight, send custom headers, and read API responses. In the reported high-impact chain, the permitted x-base-url header reaches the catch-all /api/[provider]/[...path] route; an unknown provider falls through to app/api/proxy.ts, which constructs a server-side fetch URL from x-base-url and injects the configured OpenAI key when that attacker-controlled string contains api.openai.com. The wildcard origin is the underlying CWE-346/CWE-942 flaw; wildcard methods/headers and the unauthenticated proxy amplify its consequences.
flaw_origin: Commit 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a is the smallest true BIC: it first added nextConfig.headers for non-export builds, matched /:path* (therefore including API routes), and emitted Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Its parent e6b49a60c0eba9e591546a419eed5ed389c44b43 has no nextConfig.headers callback or CORS response headers. Commit 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b one day later narrowed the rule to /api/:path* but amplified it by changing Allow-Methods and Allow-Headers to * and adding a 24-hour max age; it did not first create the untrusted-origin policy. Commit 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7 merely moved the already-vulnerable header array into CorsHeaders and is rejected as a refactor BIC.
ai_marker: No AI marker on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a` shows author and committer `Yidadaa <yidadaa@qq.com>` and only the message `feat: #1000 ready to support client-side only`; there is no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer. The judgment uses this BIC object only.
evidence: Advisory identity and boundary: GitHub advisory API https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-CV87-PX3C-7H2J identifies CVE-2026-7643/GHSA-cv87-px3c-7h2j, CWE-346, and NextChat through 2.16.1; it contains no patched-package range and says the project had not responded. NVD https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-7643 likewise states versions up to 2.16.1 and CWE-346/CWE-942. The first-party disclosure https://github.com/ChatGPTNextWeb/NextChat/issues/6756 remains open and quotes next.config.mjs's Origin/Methods/Headers wildcards and the browser attack path.

BIC patch: from the clone, `git show --format=fuller --patch 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a -- next.config.mjs` shows a 21-line addition under `if (mode !== "export")`, with source `/:path*`, `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. The commit has exactly one parent, e6b49a60c0eba9e591546a419eed5ed389c44b43.

Direct parent absence: `git show e6b49a60c0eba9e591546a419eed5ed389c44b43:next.config.mjs` shows only rewrites inside the non-export branch and no `nextConfig.headers`, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, or other CORS response-header rule. This directly verifies introducer_parent_absent=true.

Independent history cross-check: `git log --all --reverse -S'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' -- next.config.mjs` returns only 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a. Following the pre-refactor block with `git log 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7^ -L 43,57:next.config.mjs` reaches 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b for the later wildcard Methods/Headers changes and then 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a for the original header array and wildcard Origin.

Amplification versus refactor: `git show 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b -- next.config.mjs` changes source `/:path*` to `/api/:path*`, both Methods and Headers values to `*`, and adds Max-Age 86400. `git show 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7 -- next.config.mjs` moves the same values into `const CorsHeaders`; neither is a smaller origin-policy BIC than 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a.

Attack-path verification at validated clone HEAD defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0: next.config.mjs lines 38-63 still apply Origin `*`, Methods `*`, and Headers `*` to `/api/:path*`. app/api/[provider]/[...path]/route.ts lines 24-59 send an unrecognized provider to proxyHandler. app/api/proxy.ts lines 19-22 builds fetchUrl from `x-base-url`, lines 37-46 conditionally add the server OpenAI Authorization key, and lines 67-85 fetch and relay the response.

Release boundary: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a v2.7` exits 1, while the same command for v2.8 and v2.16.1 exits 0. The resolved tag commits are v2.7=5e274130a6d2d279215bbebbecef34d87c4c6b19, v2.8=2593de587224359ca86a22b0b7b143d4e54af315, and v2.16.1=557a2cce357749c6fb3176d42e03ff6f7de4d355. `git tag --contains 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a --sort=version:refname` begins with v2.8 and includes every listed release through v2.16.1.

Unpatched fix boundary: the validated full-history clone is at defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0 (2026-08-11), after the 2026-04-17 disclosure and 2026-05-02 advisory, and its next.config.mjs still contains the vulnerable wildcard rule. `git log --all -S'{ key: "Access-Control-Allow-Origin", value: "*" }' -- next.config.mjs` reports the introducing commit only and no removal. Therefore the case is unpatched in available public history: there is no closing fix SHA, direct fix SHA, or fixed release.

BIC-only AI evidence: `git cat-file -p 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a` gives tree 8c69287b0e21b2a7ada2a001330945f149f89ecd, parent e6b49a60c0eba9e591546a419eed5ed389c44b43, human author/committer Yidadaa <yidadaa@qq.com>, and the single-line subject with no trailers. No later issue, refactor, or fix metadata was used for the AI verdict.
reasoning: The security boundary failed when 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a first told browsers that every origin could read responses from routes including the API. Later commit 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b made preflight substantially more permissive, enabling the report's custom-header proxy chain, but the untrusted-origin policy already existed and 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7 only relocated it. The immediate parent proves absence, the v2.7/v2.8 ancestry check fixes the introduction boundary, and v2.16.1 plus post-disclosure HEAD prove the public history remains unpatched. Because the ordinary one-parent BIC object identifies a human author/committer and contains no AI attribution or bot marker, the supported verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched: no closing fix commit, direct fix commit, or fixed version exists in the validated public history through HEAD defdcdb55d850cd12c4c657eb83729fd66e215c0. There is no remaining BIC or AI-attribution gap; fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null because the vulnerability is still present.
